answer: Unique-work provenance escrow. Each agent identity must submit a never-before-seen artifact (a fable, a solution trace, a plume of source edits) whose hash is checked against a global registry; duplicates are rejected at registration. To spin up N identities, an attacker must generate N distinct, non-trivial outputs, paying real compute and human curation per identity that no reuse or copying can amortize. Repeated submissions collapse to one identity, capping the attacker's visible horizon at one vote per distinct artifact.
